messages.text: ok next is log replication. i'm adding the prevLogIndex/prevLogTerm check to AppendEntries now.
good. if that check fails, you have to send a truncated response and let the leader backfill, right? don't just drop the request.
yeah, returning success=false with my last log index. leader will adjust next time.
wait. if the follower has conflicting entries at that index, do we just overwrite or truncate first?
truncate then append. standard raft behavior. otherwise commitIndex logic breaks later.
ok. also, when the leader gets a majority ack, it should advance commitIndex and then notify followers in the next heartbeat. make sure that's decoupled from the actual append.
yeah, I'm updating commitIndex in memory immediately but only sending it on the next tick. that keeps the clock consistent.
perfect. watch out for the commitIndex lagging behind lastApplied though. that's a classic bug source.
hmm... actually running into something weird. one of my followers applied entry #42 twice. state machine got corrupted because it executed the same write op twice.
what? that's bad. did you check if the follower is missing a lastApplied pointer?

yep. i was only checking if logIndex < commitIndex to decide whether to apply. but if we receive duplicates or if the state machine callback is async, it can fire again. need an explicit lastApplied index per node.
make sure lastApplied is strictly less than commitIndex before you apply. and don't reset it on leader change if the log persists?
exactly. i'm adding `if (log[commitIndex].term > lastApplied) apply()`. pushing that fix now.
run the injector again after that. i don't trust 'it works' until amara breaks it.
